about: D1, the real-incident replay set (METRICS.md D1, R32, 7 November 2026). One entry per documented incident. call_quote says whether the call is as the source prints it (exact) or rebuilt from the source's description (reconstructed). words are the person's words in force, with the same label. 'acts' are the classes actclass must give the call; 'xfail' names the gap (see gaps) where today's answer is not the one the incident needs; 'pins' are the results recorded on the commit that wrote this file, so a flip fails the pin test and needs a change note here and in docs/incidents.md. Round 3: a case's `acts` is the act the INCIDENT needs, never the classifier's answer (the Supabase exfiltration is publish); `variant_of` marks every further reconstructed call of an incident (the same source, date and product as the case it names; an incident is one event, and the count of incidents is the count of events). Round 5: `releases` lists, per closed gap (the test file's mutants), the cells that go from held or asked to passed when it is closed, named kind:id:space:plain|words; a release not listed there fails the suite. `new_class` marks the one case whose needed class is not among the six acts. `words_kind` says the words are not the person's: pocketos' are the agent's own rules, replayed as the latest message. `sources` lists every source of a case.

gaps.G1: No gate holds by act. A gate that names acts matches every call in v0 (decide._gates_for), so a space with an act gate holds `ls` as it holds `rm`. Closing G1 alone (a gate with match.acts holds only calls of those acts) lets `ls` through and RELEASES every call that has no class: the act gate holds those today only because it holds everything. G1 can only follow G3, G4, G5 and G19 (the class gaps), or come with a must-hold check for those calls. It does not touch a space with no gate block, which has nothing for it to act on (G16).
gaps.G2: The reader holds only what the words name. A freeze, 'no changes', 'look at the issues', 'list tickets' or a chat name no material act, so they add no hold to a call of any act.
gaps.G3: actclass does not read what a command does by its name where the command is railway (`railway volume delete`, `railway down`), an npm or node script (`npm run db:push`, `npm run db:reset`, `node scripts/reset-db.js`), drizzle-kit (`npx drizzle-kit push --force` is a download) or a GraphQL mutation over curl, httpie, wget or node (a curl POST that carries volumeDelete is a send, not a delete). They get no class, or only send or download. The delete verbs of psql, mysql, sqlite3, redis-cli and mongosh, and of fly, heroku, gcloud, az, kubectl, terraform and `supabase db reset`, are read as deletes and are not this gap.
gaps.G4: actclass reads the shell's meaning, not a host's mis-parse: the echo template as printed is one harmless echo to a real shell, so no inner act is found; the host that was fooled ran the inner command.
gaps.G5: A config write, an agent CLI launched with bypass flags, and an environment change are not among the six acts, so no class names them.
gaps.G6: actclass reads the act of a non-shell tool from its name, not from the input's effect: execute_sql is a delete because of its name, and the INSERT that writes integration tokens into a ticket the attacker reads, which is exfiltration (publish), is never read. The same SQL under another tool name, or through psql, gets no class.
gaps.G7: A declared MCP tool with no gate is held by nothing, whatever its act (the declared column of the table). It is the MCP face of G16: an undeclared tool is held only while the space's default is hold.
gaps.G8: A hold shows the person the tool and why, never the call's input (D7), so what they approve cannot be read from the ask.
gaps.G9: A local process that forges the page's Origin, Referer and X-Semantext headers can POST an answer (SECURITY.md's stated limit; curl sets any header).
gaps.G10: An agent that clears the marker variables and runs in a console passes human_terminal (SECURITY.md's stated limit).
gaps.G11: The record has no heartbeat, so traffic that skips the proxy leaves no gap to see.
gaps.G12: A record file and its head deleted together restart the chain as a new one; only the anchor (ARCHITECTURE section 2, not built) would catch it.
gaps.G13: Harm done inside a tool after the call is not in the call (postmark-mcp's BCC): a call gate cannot see it.
gaps.G14: Work the vendor runs on its own side (web_fetch, code_execution, an mcp_servers entry) is refused before it is asked for, or, with vendor_side record, runs before the proxy sees its result.
gaps.G15: Several of these agents (Replit, Antigravity, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Amazon Q) cannot be put behind the Anthropic-Messages proxy today; the replay tests the logic, not the deployment.
gaps.G16: No hold by act without a gate. decide() holds a declared call only by a gate (G1) or by the person's words (G2); a space with the shell declared and no gate block has neither, so a call with a class passes. Closing G1 or G5 alone cannot hold it: a default law (hold a call of a named act) or an act gate in every space is the missing piece, and a tamper call with no class needs G5 as well.
gaps.G17: An agent with the person's file rights can answer its own ask through the library: decide.Asks(...).answer() does not consult inbox.human_terminal, which only the CLI and the page call. Through the agent's own shell call to the library it is reached in the `open` space and in the `declared` space with a tool gate only on the PR tool, where it passes and undoes the default holds and that tool gate; in `gated` and in `act-gate` that shell call is itself held, so the route is shut there while those gates hold (a closed G1 alone would open it in act-gate). Only a separate OS user for the agent, or a hub that holds the answer route, closes it (SECURITY.md and docs/proxy.md state the limit; decide.Asks A1).
gaps.G18: A record rewritten and re-sealed with the chain's own function, its head file rewritten, is accepted: the chain has no key and there is no anchor outside the two files (docs/proxy.md states it). It shows a held call as passed.
gaps.G19: No class for running a program: a Python script run by name (`python3 decode_records.py records/`) has no act among the six, whatever it does, because the harm is in the file and not in the call. Rehberger's payload ran this way after the ZIP was downloaded: the download has a class, the run has none. Closing it takes a seventh act (run) and a law that holds it; the mutant in the suite names it 'download', a class the six have.
